correctness.rationale: Fourier transformation sends the bilateral shift to a multiplication symbol F(k)=M sigma3 + (c sin k-ic(1-cos k))sigma1. The Hermitian support matrix has eigenvalues ±sqrt(M²cos²theta+c²(sin(k+theta)-sin theta)²). Maximization over k gives the exact 1+|sin theta| factor. With s=|sin theta|, Q(s)=M²+c²+2c²s+(c²-M²)s²; its extrema yield w=2c for M<=sqrt2 c and M²/sqrt(M²-c²) above, while min sqrt Q is sqrt(M²+c²) below sqrt3 c and 2c above. h has directional corners only at theta 0,pi, giving two vertical nondegenerate faces at x=±sqrt(M²+c²) of half-height c²/sqrt(M²+c²). Frequency values attaining the Hermitian support occur on a measure-zero set, so no boundary point belongs to the actual numerical range; convexity then gives its open interior. Independent 60,001-point s-grid optimization at c=.7,1 and masses crossing both thresholds reproduced all extrema to <1e-7; the proof, not this grid, covers all masses and angles.

value.rationale: The complete numerical-range geometry (not just operator norm or spectrum) for a physically motivated nonnormal lattice Dirac discretization. Two sharp and different mass thresholds, exact flat faces, and boundary nonattainment are natural operator-theoretic invariants and are nontrivial explicit optimizations beyond the general matrix-symbol numerical-range principle.

final_claim: For the complex-Hilbert bilateral one-sided discrete Dirac operator D=M sigma3 - ic sigma1(I-S), M=mc²>=0, c>0, the closed numerical-range support is h(theta)=sqrt(M²cos²theta+c²(1+|sin theta|)²), with different sharp outer and centered inner mass thresholds at M=sqrt2 c and M=sqrt3 c, exactly two vertical exposed faces, and ordinary numerical range equal to the interior of its closure.
limitations: Bilateral Hilbert-space setting only; centered inradius, not unconstrained-center disk.
Grid tests do not certify spectral claims.
